heroSummary: The Creality K1 Max is fully capable of printing abrasive Siraya Tech ABS-GF out of the box thanks to its stock hardened steel nozzle and fully enclosed chamber. You can achieve reliable, warp-free prints at speeds up to 179 mm/s while respecting the material's 15 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow limit.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of PVA glue stick or Magigoo release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed cap to 15 mm³/s in the Filament Settings to prevent extrusion bottlenecks at high toolhead velocities.
Configure Part Cooling Fan to 0% for standard layers, allowing a threshold of up to 20% only on bridges and overhangs steeper than 50 degrees.
Enable a 5mm outer-only brim and enforce a bed pre-soak by heating the bed to 100°C for 15 minutes prior to printing to stabilize chamber temperature.
Tune Pressure Advance to approximately 0.038 s and set Retraction Distance to 0.6 mm at 35 mm/s to eliminate stringing without causing extruder jams.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Warping or corner lifting from the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Insufficient chamber air temperature and low first layer thermal retention caused by premature heat dissipation.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Preheat the bed to 100°C with the enclosure closed for 15 minutes before starting, keep the auxiliary side fan completely disabled, and apply PVP glue stick.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Toolhead exceeding the 15 mm³/s volumetric flow limit or glass fibers causing micro-clogs in thermal transitions.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Cap print speed to 179 mm/s (or lower volumetric rate to 14 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer), increase nozzle temperature to 265°C, and ensure filament is thoroughly dried.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough outer surface finish with tiny voids and excessive stringing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in the hygroscopic ABS-GF resin vaporizing inside the melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool in a filament dryer at 75°C to 80°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, and print directly from a sealed dry box.

faq.question: Can the stock Creality K1 Max nozzle handle glass-fiber reinforced filament?
faq.answer: Yes. The Creality K1 Max comes equipped with a stock hardened steel nozzle tip designed specifically to resist the severe abrasive wear of glass and carbon-filled filaments.

faq.question: Does Siraya Tech ABS-GF require an active chamber heater on the K1 Max?
faq.answer: No. While the K1 Max lacks active chamber heating, preheating the heated bed to 100°C for 15-20 minutes builds an internal ambient temperature of 40-50°C, which is sufficient to mitigate warping.

faq.question: Should the auxiliary chamber side fan and rear exhaust fan run during printing?
faq.answer: No. Both the large auxiliary side cooling fan and the rear chamber exhaust fan should be turned completely off in OrcaSlicer to prevent draft-induced layer delamination and warping.

faq.question: Why is glue stick required on a textured PEI sheet for ABS-GF?
faq.answer: Glue stick acts as an essential release interface; ABS-GF adheres aggressively to bare PEI when hot and can tear the PEI coating off the steel sheet during removal if no release agent is applied.
